newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal, China business executives to meet next week.
newsitem.headline: Nepal, China business executives to meet next week.

text.p: Investors from Nepal and China will meet in Nepal's capital next week to promote joint ventures in the Himalayan kingdom, business executives said on Thursday.
They said the first meeting of the Nepal-China Non-Governmental Economic Cooperation Forum beginning on October 30 would identify problems in trade and investment.
"Our aim is to promote investment between the two countries," Pradeep Kumar Shrestha, vice president of the Federation of the Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industries (FNCCI), told Reuters.
"Basically we want investment promotion in Nepal through joint-venture projects."
A high-level business delegation led by Zhang Xuwu, executive vice-chairman of All China Federation of Industry and Commerce (ACFIC), was scheduled to arrive on October 29 for the two-day meeting.
The forum, set up in April during a visit by Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba to Beijing, aims to promote economic cooperation between the two neighbours.
The Chinese delegation will include leading business executives and investors.

Nepali officials said joint-venture proposals with China in the fields of mining, cement, infrastructure, hydro-electricity, textiles, light engineering, agro-based industries and pharmaceuticals would be discussed.

Nepal's trade deficit with China increased to $52.9 million in the 1994/95 fiscal year which ended in mid-July 1995, up from $43.7 million in 1993/94. Nepal's imports from China were valued at $57.6 million in 1994/95 against exports of $4.7 million.
